page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 16 vCPUs and 192 GB of RAM. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing KVM virtualization. It features a shared CPU allocation model with 16 physical cores and a single thread per core. Graphics and parallel computing workloads are handled by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and gzip/bzip3 single-threaded compression operations ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is also strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory performance is robust, with large-block read-only bandwidth reaching 223.85 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. For AI workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 339.34 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM model.

The server offers a high-density memory profile of 12 GB per core alongside dedicated GPU acceleration, presenting a balanced resource layout for memory-intensive and parallel computing tasks. However, the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability under sustained, highly intensive CPU-only workloads. The lack of local storage requires external volume attachments for data persistence. This configuration is well-suited for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, memory-heavy analytical processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering workloads.
